title: Age Bands Applied to Lift Ticket Pricing
content:
Four age bands are priced below the adult price across the whole Lift Tickets line, and each band takes its own share of that adult price. The shares and the ages that define the bands stand alike on every product in the line, from the Granite Ridge Window Day Ticket through the two advance tickets and the two flex packs to the Granite Ridge Collective Multi-Mountain Ticket Pack.

| Band | Share of the adult price | Age parameter, in whole years |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Child | 55 percent | oldest age priced as a child: 6 |
| Youth | 80 percent | oldest age priced as a youth: 17 |
| Senior | 85 percent | youngest age priced as a senior: 65 |
| Super senior | 50 percent | youngest age priced as a super senior: 80 |

Each figure in the middle column is the percentage of the adult price charged for a ticket in that band. Each figure in the right-hand column is the age in whole years that bounds the band: for the child and youth bands it is the oldest age the band still carries, and for the senior and super senior bands it is the youngest age at which the band is reached.

## Points of judgement on the boundaries

- A holder of 6 whole years falls within the child band, that being the oldest age priced as a child; a holder of 7 whole years does not.
- A holder of 17 whole years falls within the youth band, that being the oldest age priced as a youth; a holder of 18 whole years does not.
- A holder of 64 whole years has not reached the senior band; a holder of 65 whole years has, that being the youngest age priced as a senior.
- A holder of 79 whole years has not reached the super senior band; a holder of 80 whole years has, that being the youngest age priced as a super senior.

Because the bands are set in whole years, a part year is disregarded in reading the table: a holder in their seventh year of age is read as 6 whole years until the seventh birthday.
